title: Shared definitions
description: Identifiers and value types shared by every Elabora schema.

slug.description: Identifier for course elements (screens, blocks, layers, free objects, events). Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. Must be unique in the whole course. Ids are permanent: learner progress is keyed by id, so rename one only with elabora rename, which rewrites every reference and keeps its key in elabora.lock.json.

planId.description: Identifier of a plan element (objective, item, locked text, question, source). Uppercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, for example OBJ-2, ITEM-5, TXT-3, Q-12, SRC-1.

variableId.description: Variable identifier: starts with a lowercase letter, then letters, digits or underscores (camelCase or snake_case).

markdown.description: Text in the Elabora Markdown subset: paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, lists, tables, links, `code`, line breaks, and maths in LaTeX between $…$ (inline) or $$…$$ (display), rendered as MathML at build time. Raw HTML is not rendered. Images must use image blocks, not Markdown.

patchOperation.description: One operation of a JSON Patch (RFC 6902), as elabora plan write --patch and MCP elabora_write_plan take it.

assetPath.description: Path of a file inside the course assets/ folder, relative to assets/ (for example images/router.png). ASCII letters, digits, '-', '_', '.', '/' only, so every LMS accepts the file name.

focus.description: Focal point of an image: where its subject is, from 0 (left, top) to 1 (right, bottom). An image cropped to fit its place (a band, a grid cell, a phone) keeps this point in view; without it, the crop keeps the middle.

x.description: Across, from the left edge (0) to the right edge (1).

y.description: Down, from the top edge (0) to the bottom edge (1).

color.description: Colour as a 6-digit hex value, for example #12355B.

pronunciations.description: Words a generated voice says otherwise than they are written, by language tag: each text (a whole word or phrase, case-sensitive) is said as say. Captions and the transcript keep the text.

text.description: As written in the lines (P-12, 9 h 30).

say.description: As the voice should say it (pé douze, neuf heures trente).

voiceLine.description: A line a voice says: the common shape of the lines of a screen's narration, of a layer's narration and of a dialogue. Its id is unique in the screen, every track counted (the screen's narration, each layer's, each dialogue's): cues, translations and the line's audio files (assets/narration/<language>/<screen>/<line>.m4a) are named by it. The schemas that use it add their own fields and close it (unevaluatedProperties).

id.description: Unique in the screen, every track counted (l1, l2…): cues, translations and the line's audio files are named by it.

speaker.description: A speaker of course.json speakers, named in the captions and the transcript. Default: the first speaker of the course (none: no name).

text.description: What the voice says, word for word: the captions and the transcript. Do not show the same words on screen (E4, W_NARRATION_DUPLICATED). Words in square brackets are stage directions for an expressive voice ([chuchote], [rit], [un temps]: how to say it, where the delivery changes): never shown nor counted as words; a voice that cannot play them says the line without them.

delivery.description: How a generated voice says this line, by language (it is translated): settings of the voice tool (speed, style…) over those of the speaker's voice in that language, for example { "fr": { "speed": 1.1 } }. Other settings make the line's audio out of date.

pronunciations.description: How a generated voice says words of this line, by language, before those of the course.

anchor.description: A moment of the screen's timeline or of a layer's (docs/decisions.md D62), written against what the voice says rather than in seconds, so that it holds when a voice is generated again, recorded or translated: a line ({ "line": "l2" }), a word or a few words of it ({ "line": "l2", "word": "imprimante" }), the end of either (edge end), shifted by offset seconds. On a screen without narration, seconds from the start of a step ({ "seconds": 1.5 }); on a layer without narration, seconds from its opening. The start or the end of a step's stretch of the timeline ({ "step": 2 }, { "step": 2, "edge": "end" }).

line.description: A line of the screen's narration (narration.lines[].id), or, for a block or a cue of a layer, of that layer's narration (layers[].narration.lines[].id): an anchor stays on its own timeline (E_TIMELINE_ANCHOR_TRACK).

word.description: One or a few words of the line, as written there (case, punctuation and apostrophes aside): the moment the voice says them. Their time comes from the line's word times (the sidecar's words, filled by forced alignment), estimated from the text without them. Translations carry it as a marker that translators place on the words of their language. A word no longer in the line is an error (E_TIMELINE_ANCHOR_MISSING); editing the line's text moves the anchor with its word.

occurrence.description: Which time the word appears in the line, when it appears more than once.

edge.description: start: when the line, the word or the step starts. end: when it ends.

offset.description: Seconds after the line or the word (negative: before).

seconds.description: Screens without narration only: seconds from the start of a step (step, else the block's step, else 1); in a layer without narration, from its opening. Narrated screens and layers anchor to their lines and words.

step.description: With seconds: the step they count from. Alone: the start of that step's stretch of the timeline, or its end with edge end.

moment.description: When a timed block appears (timing.in) or leaves (timing.out), and how.

effect.description: How it comes or goes: none (at once), fade, rise (moves up a few pixels while fading in), slide (from direction), zoom, wipe (uncovered from direction), draw (the strokes of its drawing are drawn; a wipe for blocks without one), or an effect of the course's theme (course.json theme.effects). Effects move the block relative to its place, never the layout. Default: fade (the transition of a pile for its contents). Under reduced motion every effect becomes a short fade, at the same times.

duration.description: Seconds the effect lasts. Default: 0.4 (fade, zoom), 0.5 (rise, slide), 0.6 (wipe), 1.2 (draw), 0.4 for theme effects.

direction.description: slide and wipe: where the block comes from (default left: it slides in from the left, or is uncovered from left to right).

language.description: BCP 47 language tag, for example fr, en, fr-FR.

numericTolerance.description: Accepted distance from the expected value: absolute (same unit as the answer) or percent of the answer. Without tolerance only the exact value is accepted.

percent.description: Accept answer ± this percentage of the answer.

numericFeedback.description: Elaborated feedback of a numeric question (guardrail D1): why the expected value is right, and what to check when the answer is wrong.

incorrect.description: Shown for wrong values that match no misconception.

activityFeedback.description: Feedback of a fill-in or sort activity (guardrail D1): correct says why the answer holds, incorrect what to look at again. Shown under the activity once it is submitted; without incorrect feedback, W_ACTIVITY_NO_FEEDBACK.

incorrect.description: Shown while some answers are wrong: explain the rule or the clue, without giving the answers (they show in place after the last try).

misconceptions.description: Values learners get with a typical error, each with feedback that names the error. They are checked before the generic incorrect feedback.

aspectRatio.description: Shape of an embedded frame. auto: the free object sets its own height (host.requestHeight). fill: the frame fills the height of its layout slot.

mediaQuality.description: Preset of the media shipped in a package: high (the masters), medium or low (renditions encoded from the masters, for LMS size limits).
